solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dairy product from goat?

definitions.meaning: a goat is something that butts, so playfully one that butts

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: a goat is a creature that butts things, so it is a 'butter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Churned cream gives the spread, and an animal that rams with its head is jokingly named for that action.

clue.text: Tiny stream and little river featured in short publication

indicators.note: featured in means placed within the following word

parts.note: a booklet is a short publication
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A small brook and a minor river appear in a pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brook is a tiny stream; the suffix marks it as little.

clue.text: The two at opposite ends that will never meet famous author?

definitions.text: The two at opposite ends that will never meet
definitions.meaning: from Kipling's line about East and West; an old word for two

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling wrote that East and West are two that never meet; the archaic word for two there is also an American writer's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a pair, and the pen name of the creator of Tom Sawyer.

clue.text: Groups of buildings in eastern countries?

parts.note: states are countries

explanation.surface: Housing developments springing up in Asian nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Housing or industrial developments are planned groups of buildings.

clue.text: Conservative moves to a higher plane in desperate situations

parts.note: something that moves to a higher plane goes up, i.e. rises

explanation.surface: A Tory politician achieves spiritual elevation while everything around is in turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonym: turning points of acute danger or difficulty are desperate situations.

clue.text: Full service in gym following Religious Education

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after Religious Education

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education

indicators.note: in means put inside the gym abbreviation

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
a let is a tennis serve that must be replayed

explanation.surface: A school timetable has a complete service in the gym after Religious Education.
explanation.walkthrough: RE and PE are school subjects; a LET is a tennis service that clips the net and is retaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: replete means filled to capacity, especially with food.

clue.text: Sort of match that could make fan smile — gripping one

indicators.note: gripping means holding something inside
could make suggests the letters can be made into something new

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grinning supporter clutches a ticket for a big game.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports match whose winners go through to the final is a type of match.

clue.text: Small bag with a cold explosive hidden in street

indicators.note: hidden in means the following pieces are placed inside the word for street

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A small packet containing a chilly bomb is concealed in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sealed packet holding a single portion is a small bag.

clue.text: Caesar possibly twitching, as he was with Cleopatra

parts.note: Julius Caesar is an example of a Roman, hence 'possibly'
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar fidgets nervously, just as he did during his affair with the Egyptian queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: Caesar's relationship with Cleopatra was a famous love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being amorous or loving describes how Caesar behaved in his celebrated affair with the Egyptian queen.

clue.text: Reduce atmospheric pollution to try and reduce tension

definitions.meaning: literally to make the atmosphere cleaner
idiom for settling a dispute by talking it through

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for easing a strained mood literally describes purifying the atmosphere.

clue.text: Stuff that slushy and fruity from British star down under?

parts.note: a Pom is Australian slang for a British person, which 'down under?' signals
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: Something mushy and fruity comes from a British celebrity living in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under?' tells you the word for British is the Australian one: POM.
explanation.definitionFit: The pulpy residue left after crushing apples or grapes is slushy fruit matter.

clue.text: Protective covering is missing from a finch

indicators.note: the word 'is' is to be left out of the bird's name

parts.note: a siskin is a small finch

explanation.surface: A finch has lost its protective plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer of an animal's body is its natural protective covering.

clue.text: Subsequently dealt with awful threat — free!

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are handled and rearranged
something awful is in a bad state, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Once the frightful menace has been handled, we are free at last!
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt with' and 'awful' both signal rearranging THREAT and FREE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: after that time, or afterwards, means subsequently.

clue.text: Medical specialist ungenerous or nasty

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are messed up and reordered

explanation.surface: A doctor is described as either stingy or unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon who operates on the brain and nervous system is a medical specialist.

clue.text: It's awfully dry with heater? Get some moisture back in

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A heater makes things terribly dry, so you need to add moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore lost water to something is to put moisture back in.

clue.text: Farm animals given help, we hear, in form of defence against invaders

parts.note: livestock on a farm are called stock

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Livestock receive assistance in building a barrier against raiders.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the 'help' part changes spelling when said aloud: AID sounds like the ending ADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive barrier of upright timber posts is a fortification against invaders.

clue.text: Old pop group that will often get drunk late at night!

definitions.meaning: a British soul and pop band of the 1970s, known for 'You Sexy Thing'

definitions.text: that will often get drunk late at night!
definitions.meaning: a warm cocoa drink is often had at bedtime

explanation.walkthrough: 'get drunk' hints at alcohol, but the drink is a soothing bedtime cocoa.
explanation.definitionFit: The band of that name shares it with the warm cocoa beverage commonly sipped before bed.

clue.text: More than one young choirboy quivers, wanting to avoid Mass

indicators.note: wanting to avoid means leaving out the letter for Mass

parts.note: trembles means quivers

explanation.surface: A young chorister shakes with nerves, hoping to skip church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a church service but is just M, the physics symbol for mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Boy singers with the highest voices in a choir are high voices, plural.

clue.text: Language of tribe including a word for 'thanks'

indicators.note: including means holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: a clan is a tribe or extended family group
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A tribe's tongue includes a special word for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romance tongue spoken in north-east Spain is a language.

clue.text: Animal not in sty? Put it away

definitions.meaning: a pig that is out of its pen
idiom for eating a lot greedily

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase describes a hog that has escaped its pen; as an idiom it means to gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb for eating greedily matches the slang 'put it away'.

clue.text: Deadliest man initially trained in this part of the world?

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of man
trained suggests the letters are moulded into a new shape

explanation.surface: The most lethal fighter was trained in this troubled region.
explanation.definitionFit: The region spanning south-west Asia and Egypt is a part of the world.

clue.text: Fairy one's sometimes seen sliding over ice

definitions.meaning: the mischievous sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.text: one's sometimes seen sliding over ice
definitions.meaning: the rubber disc hit in ice hockey

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's mischievous sprite shares a name with the ice hockey disc.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprite of Shakespeare's comedy and the hard rubber disc of ice hockey share one name.

clue.text: Musician's publication that is read out in Australia?

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: said in a broad Australian accent, where the vowel shifts

parts.note: a paper is a publication

explanation.surface: A musician's newspaper is recited aloud by someone in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: In a broad Australian accent 'paper' is said with the vowel of 'pie'.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of bagpipes or a pipe is a musician.

clue.text: Extra announcement that would have disappointed the ugly sisters

definitions.meaning: in cricket an extra is a run given away, such as one for an illegal delivery

definitions.text: announcement that would have disappointed the ugly sisters
definitions.meaning: Cinderella's stepsisters longed to attend the ball, so news it was cancelled would upset them

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery, scored as an extra run; read as 'no ball', it is bad news for Cinderella's stepsisters.
explanation.definitionFit: An illegal cricket delivery adds a run as an extra, and saying 'no dance' would dash pantomime hopes.

clue.text: Various characters in rep, loyal in performance

indicators.note: the letters found in the next words are mixed into various orders

explanation.surface: A faithful actor plays several different parts in repertory theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like theatre roles but means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting out a part, as in a training exercise, is a kind of performance.

clue.text: Article is written by head of monastery: 'A form of belief'

parts.note: the is the definite article
taken as written

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of monastery

explanation.surface: A piece written by an abbot sets out a form of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of monastery' suggests an abbot, but it gives just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in the existence of a god or gods is a form of religious conviction.

clue.text: Food served in part of hospital stank, not half!

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: the second half of the word for stank is dropped

parts.note: reeked means stank

explanation.surface: The meal dished out in one hospital ward smelled terrible, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half!' reads as British slang for 'very much', but it cuts REEKED to REE.
explanation.definitionFit: A main course or dish served at a meal is food served.
